narrationScript: Welcome to Chapter 2.2: RISC versus CISC Design Philosophy. Historically, Instruction Set Architectures, or ISAs, evolved along two main paths: CISC, for Complex Instruction Set Computer, and RISC, for Reduced Instruction Set Computer. Understanding this fundamental dichotomy is crucial, as it underpins the design philosophies of virtually all modern processors. In this lesson, we'll explore the origins and characteristics of both approaches, evaluate their trade-offs, and see how these design principles shape today's dominant architectures. By the end, you'll be able to compare and contrast RISC and CISC, understand their historical evolution, describe key ISA characteristics like load-store architecture and instruction length, and evaluate the trade-offs between ISA complexity and implementation efficiency.
